notes:
VERDICT: UNMET, and NO NEW CREDIT WAS SPENT ON THIS OPTION.

WHY NOTHING WAS GENERATED. generation.json already recorded attempt=4 (candidate-4.png, job 6241bf4e, 2026-08-10T22:19Z) with no qc.json ever written. The standing instruction is a hard cap of THREE generations per option; four were already paid for by an earlier wave that then failed to log a verdict. Generating a fifth would have been exactly the runaway the brief warns about, so this pass did the free work instead: read the drawing, measured all four existing candidates, and made the already-purchased artifacts durable by writing this record.

WHAT THE DRAWING ACTUALLY SHOWS. The file is a genuine trouser tech pack (front, waistband, three belt loops), not a swatch page or a placeholder. The red highlighter marks a long, near-PLUMB slit on the front panel - x=420-495, y=280-762, 3.22 deg off vertical, 4.68 waistband-depths long, both ends free, sitting 0.45 WD below the waistband seam and 0.59 WD outboard of a long vertical reference line. Magnified 2x, the red is seen to overlay a thin black drawn line, confirming it marks a real opening. The option description's '0 deg' therefore means 0 deg from the SIDE SEAM - vertical - and not 0 deg from horizontal, which is how three of the four generations read it. The drawing also carries a separate black HORIZONTAL welt at x=628-975, y=318-398 (0.44 WD deep); the locked prompt explicitly instructs that this secondary welt be ignored, and the same welt appears in the sibling jeans-square drawing as fixed context, so its absence from the renders is correct and is not scored against them.

THE FOUR CANDIDATES. Attempts 1, 2 and 4 all render a generic horizontal besom hip welt - the drawn feature rotated by about 79 degrees. Attempt 3 is the outlier and the only good one: it renders a genuine vertical double-jetted besom, 3.90 deg off plumb against the drawn 3.22 deg, straight to within 2.5 px over 527 px, both ends closed square. Attempt 4 then discarded that and reverted to horizontal. That is oscillation, not convergence, and it is the fourth time this project has seen a correction fix its target while destroying a feature that already worked.

RECOMMENDATION FOR A HUMAN. Candidate-3 is clearly the best of the four and should be reviewed for promotion. Its remaining faults are a lateral placement error of about 1.45 waistband-depths (it sits mid-panel at 2.04 WD from the crease where the drawing puts it at 0.59 WD) and a length 11 percent short (4.15 WD against 4.68 WD). Neither is close to as damaging as attempt 4's 79-degree orientation inversion, and the length is arguably defensible: at 4.15 WD it computes to 14.5-16.6 cm, which lands inside the spec's own stated 14-16 cm band, whereas the drawing's own 4.68 WD computes to 16-19 cm. Candidate-3 would still not pass the 98 gate on placement, so this is a judgement call for the owner, not an approval.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, STATED PLAINLY. (1) Jet count is NOT gradeable from the drawing. The highlighter covers a single thin stroke; I cannot tell whether a single-jet or double-jet besom was intended, so candidate-3's double jet is neither credited nor penalised. (2) No centimetre figure is recoverable - the tech pack carries no printed dimension callout, so every number above is a ratio against waistband depth, which is stable in the drawing (103 px +/- 0.5 across four columns) and in candidate-3 (127 px) but NOT in candidate-4 (81-107 px, because the shirt/waistband boundary will not separate cleanly there); candidate-4's length figure is therefore quoted as a range, not a point. (3) The identity of the drawing's long vertical reference line - front crease or side seam - was not assumed. I tested it by belt-loop-pitch mapping: drawing loop-1 left edge x=125.5 to loop-2 left edge x=569.5 gives a pitch of 444 px, candidate-3 gives 138 to 578 for a pitch of 440, and mapping the drawing's x=519 line through that transform predicts render x=528 against a measured crease at x=569 - an 8 percent residual, which supports the identification as the front crease but does not prove it. The placement finding survives either reading, because under both the drawn slit sits close to that line and the render puts it far away; only the wording of the correction direction depends on it. (4) I did not attempt to grade edge-stitch presence: the charcoal twill's own weave noise dominates at this resolution in every candidate.

Nothing was written to data-store/ or public/images/reports/. No craft option or existing image was deleted or modified. Measurement crops were written only to the session scratchpad, not into the repo.
